[2] Misc. Appeal No.585/2020 has been filed by the Insurance Company/appellant challenging the award dated 24.10.2019 passed by Second Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Dhar in Claims Case No.1000566/2015 whereby the non-applicant therein were directed to pay compensation of Rs. 1,
32,332/- to the appellant therein jointly and severally on account of injuries sustained due to accident.

sentences.text: [3] These Misc. Appeals arises out common accident dated 28.10.2014, thus these Appeals are being disposed of by this common judgment.

Facts of the case in short, are as under;-
[4] On 28.10.2014, near about 08:30, the Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP-09-CD-6989 driven by Javed Ansari and owned by Gulam Hussain which was insured by Insurance Company dashed the motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-09-QD-4958.

Due to the said accident, Yasin,
Wazid died and Mehmood suffered injuries.

The legal heirs of Yasin and parents of Wazid filed Claim Case No.229/2015 & 230/2015 seeking compensation of Rs.21,50,000/- and 16,50,000/-
respectively.
Likewise, injured Mehmood filed Claim Case No.1000566/2015 seeking compensation of Rs.13,25,000/-.
[5] After the aforesaid incident, an FIR was lodged at Police Station- Pithampur on 29.10.2014 on an information given by Nilesh Kumar against unknown person and vehicle.
Later on, the police found that Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP-09-CD-6989 was driven by Javed Ansari at the time of incident.
Accordingly, Javed Ansari was arrested on 18.12.2014 and the Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP- 09-CD-6989 was seized by the police vide seizure memo dated 18.10.2014.
The notice under Section 133 of M.V.Act was issued to the owner of Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP-09-CD-6989 i.e. Gulam Hussain.
He appeared before the Station House Officer and admitted that his driver Javed was driving Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP-09-CD-6989 and caused the accident.

The Police seized the Insurance Policy and Driving License and filed the Charge- sheet before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Dhar under Section The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Mehmood @ Babu on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101500718/
4 279, 337,338 and 304 (A) of IPC.
[6] In the claim case, entire Charge-sheet was exhibited alongwith alongwith other medical documents.

sentences.text: The Insurance Company contested the claim by submitting the reply to the effect that the Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP-09-CD-6989 has been falsely implicated in this case in order to get compensation.
The incident was not caused by the Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP-09-CD-6989 as per the report submitted by Sisodiya Investigation.
Before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, the Dilip Singh Sisodia was appeared as witness of Insurance Company.
In cross examination, he admits that while preparing report, he did not go to the spot and on the basis of papers, he prepared report.
He also admits that he did not take the statement of any independent witness.

The learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal discarded the aforesaid report and held the Insurance Company to pay the compensation, hence, these Misc. Cases before this Court solely on the ground that the vehicle has been falsely implicated in this case.
I have heard learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

[7] It is correct that initially an FIR was lodged an unknown vehicle and person and informant did not disclose the registration number of the offending vehicle but in the investigation, the police found that the accident caused by this particular vehicle i.e. Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP-09-CD-6989.

The owner of the Bolero Jeep bearing registration No.MP-09-CD-6989 was called upon to the Police Station who admitted the accident from his vehicle, therefore, there is no reason to doubt the investigation conducted by the Police.

Even in case of FIR lodged against an unknown person, the Police after investigation, on the basis of evidence collected during the investigation implicate the accuse in the FIR, therefore, it cannot be said that the driver and vehicle have falsely been implicated.

In the present case, nothing has been produced to show that the driver has been acquitted from the charges under Section 279,
337,338 and 304 (A) of IPC.
The police is having power to conduct the investigation under the provision of Code of Criminal Procedure and I have no reason to doubt with the investigation conducted by the Police.
Even otherwise, the information was not given by claimants as well as injured to the Police.
The information was given by a third person who was present on the spot.
Even if, he did not disclose the registration number of the offending vehicle, the claimants and injured cannot be denied for compensation.

[8] In this case, there is no delay in lodging the FIR and there is also dispute that two persons ie.
Yasin and Wajid died and Mehmood was injured due to accident, thus merely the registration number of vehicle was not disclosed, the entire investigation cannot be discarded.
[9] The Apex Court in case of NCT vs. Sunil (2000) ISCC 748 the has held as under;-
"We feel that it is an archaic notion that actions of the police officer should be approached with initial distrust.
We are aware that such a notion was lavishly entertained during British period and policemen also knew about it.
Its hang over persisted during post-independent years but it is time now to start placing at least initial trust on the actions and the documents made by the police.
At any rate, the court cannot start with the presumption that the police records are untrustworthy.
As a proposition of law the presumption should be the other way around.

That official acts of the police have been regularly performed is a wise principle of presumption The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Mehmood @ Babu on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101500718/
5 and recognised even by the legislature.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence when a police officer gives evidence in court that a certain article was recovered by him on the strength of the statement made by the accused it is open to the court to believe the version to be correct if it is not otherwise shown to be unreliable.

It is for the accused, through cross-examination of witnesses or through any other materials, to show that the evidence of the police officer is either unreliable or at least unsafe to be acted upon in a particular case.

If the court has any good reason to suspect the truthfulness of such records of the police the court could certainly take into account the fact that no other independent person was present at the time of recovery.

But it is not a legally approvable procedure to presume the police action as unreliable to start with, nor to jettison such action merely for the reason that police did not collect signatures of independent persons in the documents made contemporaneous with such actions.''
[10] In view of above, I do not find any ground to interfere with the impugned awards, accordingly all the Misc. Appeal are hereby dismissed.
Office is directed to place the photocopy of this order in all the connected Misc.
Appeals.
(VIVEK RUSIA) JUDGE praveen
